verdict.rationale: Browserbase's API reference pages render a live Mintlify "Try it" playground with runnable requests to api.browserbase.com. The pages are generated from a published OpenAPI 3.0.0 document, so users can explore the API interactively and execute examples. The openapi.json probe 404s were only at guessed paths; the spec is published at /reference/api/openapi.v1.yaml, so this does not contradict the claim. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the playground, and evidence of how deep the per-endpoint examples go (e.g., multi-language code samples).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can explore an interactive API reference with runnable examples

citations.quote: The "Create a Session" API reference page renders a live "Try it" API playground (the Mintlify api.playground runtime) with a runnable request to https://api.browserbase.com/v1/sessions.
The same "Try it" control appears across the /reference/api endpoint pages, which are generated from the published OpenAPI document.
docs.browserbase.com publishes a downloadable OpenAPI 3.0.0 document whose info block reads "title: Browserbase API"
